artist.name: Henry Moodie
artist.short_description: Henry Moodie: an Afterglow editorial discovery candidate in pop.
artist.biography: Henry Moodie is a British pop singer-songwriter known for intimate, diary-like relationship songs and emotionally direct ballads. His breakout catalogue includes “you were there for me,” “drunk text,” “pick up the phone,” and “closure,” with later projects including good old days and mood swings. In interviews with GEM and EUPHORIA, Moodie discussed the writing process behind “drunk text” and explained that the song deals with feelings for a person who did not know he wanted to be more than friends. He has separately described “you were there for me” as a song about his best friend, and “eighteen” as a reflection on an uncertain stage of early adulthood. These are unusually useful firsthand references for Afterglow’s song-storytelling feature. His tracks can connect listeners of Etham and Alex Sampson to more piano-led emotional-pop material. Editorial mood tags can help visitors find his songs, but interpretations should never be substituted for his own confirmed explanations.
